t:
Subsection (b) cf section 5385 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 (relating to specially sweetened natural wines) is amended to read as follows:


“(b) 
Cellar Treatment.—
Specially sweetened natural wines may be blended with each other, or with natural wine or heavy bodied blending wine in the further production of specially sweetened natural wine only, if the wines so blended are made from the same kind of fruit. Wines produced under this section may be cellar treated under the provisions of section 5382 (a) and (c). Wine spirits may not be added to specially sweetened natural wine.”

fable.w: This section amends the Internal Revenue Code to set substantive rules on blending and cellar treatment of specially sweetened natural wines. It contains no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. There is no real tempting contrary reading, since the text only regulates how wine producers may make the product and does not bring them into any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section defines technical regulations for the production and blending of wines. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or requirements to consult with states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_block.s: Specially sweetened natural wines may be blended with each other, or with natural wine or heavy bodied blending wine in the further production of specially sweetened natural wine only, if the wines so blended are made from the same kind of fruit.

opus.w: This amendment only sets substantive rules for blending and cellar-treating specially sweetened natural wines. No one outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any federal decision. A reader might take the cross-reference to section 5382 as granting rulemaking authority, but this section does not authorize or require any regulation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Internal Revenue Code to define technical standards for blending specially sweetened natural wines. It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties (such as winemakers, the public, or state governments) before making a decision. The text merely establishes rules for production, which falls under substantive regulation rather than participatory decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: Specially sweetened natural wines may be blended with each other, or with natural wine or heavy bodied blending wine in the further production of specially sweetened natural wine only, if the wines so blended are made from the same kind of fruit.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the amendment involves "participation" because it regulates how wines are produced and blended, potentially involving winemakers. However, the text only sets forth technical standards for blending and cellar treatment. It does not require the government to consult with winemakers, the public, or any outside entity before making a decision. It is a substantive regulatory provision, not a procedural one involving external input.
